subject: Acme — Rate limits & Overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme — Rate limits & Overage pricing (post-demo recap)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + next steps around rate limits and pricing so we’re aligned before I loop in engineering: 

Key notes from our call:
- Current prod usage: ~30M tokens/day across NLU + generation routes.
- Burst pattern: periodic spikes to ~200M tokens/day for 2–6 hours during campaign pushes.
- Primary concern: avoid throttling during short bursts while keeping unit economics predictable.

Open asks for your procurement team so we can finalize a proposal:
1) Target budget range for Q2 (ballpark is fine) — helps us propose committed vs on-demand mix.
2) Target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for (we can show options for $/1M at different commit tiers).
3) Any fixed SLA or quota increase windows required for campaigns (e.g., 48hr burst grace, pre-notice required).

Attached: redwood-overage-pricing.pdf (summary), mutual-action-plan.docx (MVP timeline).

Proposed next steps:
- You share target budget and preferred $/1M target.
- I’ll send a one-page pricing option with 3 configs: Self-serve hosted (overage), Reserved capacity (committed GPU pool), and Hybrid (commit + burst buffer).
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Camila (solutions engineer) to validate quota & throughput.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for numbers and will draft the pricing options when you send them.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

--

Attachment: mutual-action-plan.docx
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme — Rate limits & Overage pricing (post-demo recap)

Thanks Marissa — great session. Quick answers below: 

- Budget range: aiming for $40k–$70k/month in Q2 for inference spend (we may grow).
- Target $/1M tokens: ideally <= $35 / 1M tokens for generation-heavy routes; embedding routes can be higher.
- Burst policy: we need short burst protection for campaign windows (we expect up to 72 hours of heavy activity across regions) — 48 hours grace would be preferred, but we can be flexible if there’s a clear overage cap.

I’ll let Procurement start the paperwork after we have a clear pricing page. Also copying Alex who owns infra/throughput.

Jordan
Dir. Product, Acme Corp
jordan.miller@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme — Rate limits & Overage pricing (post-demo recap)

Appreciate the clarity, Jordan — this is really helpful. High-level options based on what you shared: 

Option A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go + overage):
- No commit; overage priced at $45 / 1M tokens for generation routes, $60 / 1M for embeddings.
- Default quota: 50M tokens/day with burst throttles; quota increases via support request (same-day in most cases).

Option B — Reserved (committed monthly capacity):
- Commit to 1B tokens/month --> equivalent pricing ~ $30 / 1M tokens for generation when amortized.
- Includes a 48-hour grace buffer for bursts up to 3x average daily usage; predictable SLOs and priority routing.

Option C — Hybrid (commit + burst buffer):
- Mid-sized commit + a burst buffer pool charged at a blended $35 / 1M tokens.
- Automated quota increase rules for pre-notified campaigns (72hr advance preferred).

Notes on overage and burst handling:
- Short bursts: we can provision a temporary burst quota for 24–72 hours depending on capacity; temporary quota increases can be automated if you provide a campaign window and expected peak.
- Overage caps: we can set hard caps to prevent runaway charges — Procurement can pick a monthly cap.
- For procurement ease, we’ll show line items: base commit, burst buffer, and emergency overage charge.

Camila — would you be able to validate the burst capacity assumptions (200M peak) and confirm expected throughput & TCP concurrency requirements? If so, we’ll include a recommended quota/increase policy in the MAP.

If that looks good, I’ll prepare a one-pager and formal pricing grid for Procurement to review.

Best,
Marissa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Acme — Rate limits & Overage pricing (post-demo recap)

Internal note / recommended approach for the proposal: 

- Recommend we lead with Option C (Hybrid) — hits their budget midpoint and gives predictable unit economics while enabling bursts.
- Suggested pricing lines: $33 / 1M generation tokens (commit tier), $38 / 1M burst buffer, emergency overage at $60 / 1M with a hard monthly cap option.
- Quota policy: auto-grant + grace window: 48hr automatic buffer at 2x daily average; additional increases require 72hr notice.
- For Procurement asks, include a table that converts tokens -> API requests (example: average prompt+response = 1.2k tokens/request) so they can reason about request volume vs tokens.

I’ll draft the pricing grid and hand to Marissa to send to Acme. Camila — happy to sync if you want to tweak the throughput numbers before we lock pricing.

-Rafael
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Acme — Quota & burst configuration details

Hi Jordan — quick tech note from my side. I pulled the numbers you mentioned and sketched a conservative quota config we recommend for the first 90 days. Attached is a short usage snapshot CSV that will help us size the burst pool.

Proposed config:
- Base quota: 60M tokens/day distributed across US-West and US-East routes.
- Burst pool: 300M tokens/day available for up to 48 hours with automatic throttling beyond that.
- Pre-notice rule: campaigns >3x baseline require 72 hours notice to guarantee additional capacity.
- Telemetry we need from you: a sample CSV with hourly token usage for the last 14 days + example campaign windows (start/end times).

Attachment: acme-usage-snapshot.csv

If you send the CSV, I’ll run it through our sizing script and return a recommended committed amount and the minimum reserved GPU profile for the hybrid option.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
